memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But the Egyptians mistreated us and made us suffer, subjecting us to harsh labour. Then we cried out to the Lord, the God of our ancestors, and the Lord heard our voice and saw our misery, toil and oppression." — Deut 26:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The story continues, and it turns dark. Slavery, harsh labour, suffering, oppression. God's people were crushed under Egypt's cruelty for generations. But notice the turning point in the whole account: "we cried out to the Lord... and the Lord heard."

This is one of the most comforting truths in all of Scripture — our God hears. He is not distant or deaf to the suffering of His people. He saw their misery. He noticed their toil. He heard every groan. Nothing about their pain escaped His attention.

If you are in a hard season right now — worn down, mistreated, weary — take this deeply to heart. The same God who heard Israel's cry hears yours. Your tears are not falling into an empty sky. He sees your misery, your toil, your oppression, just as He saw theirs.

We do not always get an immediate answer, and the Bible never pretends the wait is easy. But the God we cry to is a God who hears, and in His time He acts. Through Christ we now come to Him boldly as our Father, knowing He listens to His children (Heb 4:16; 1 Pet 3:12).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I truly believe God hears me when I cry out?
2. What suffering do I need to bring honestly to Him today?
3. How does knowing He "sees my misery" comfort me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are the God who hears. You see my struggles and You have not forgotten me. I bring my burdens to You and trust that You are listening. Amen.
